open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” / “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created for the newly minted TrialExecutions and decided_at?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not attach the new executions
Create a new AdmissionVerdict observation for each admission run
Replace or mutate the existing verdict with the new executions
open_points.default_guess: Create a new immutable AdmissionVerdict entity for each admission run, while requiring its admitted/refused result to be deterministic for the implementation and corpus.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” / “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can be unproven before a binding is accepted and proven afterward?
options: ProofResult is a contextual observation that also depends on current binding state
ProofResult is identified by the flow version plus a snapshot or digest of proof dependencies
A flow version has only one permanent proof result
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computation as depending on the current immutable dependency state, rather than asserting that flow_version_id alone determines the result.

open_points.subject: Activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: “The current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last” and “the corpus only grows,” while rollback “must already hold an admitted verdict over the current corpus.”
open_points.question: After a new TrialCase is added, what happens to an implementation activated under the previous corpus?
options: The activation remains usable by new runs until another activation replaces it
The activation ceases to be current immediately
The activation remains recorded as current, but new runs are refused until that implementation is admitted over the enlarged corpus
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing activation usable; require current-corpus admission only when creating a later activation or rollback, because no invalidation transition is defined.

open_points.subject: Run and draft-write activation authority
open_points.text: M26 requires “the flow activation under which the run started,” but M19 records only “flow_version_id: pinned at start.”
open_points.question: How does a Run identify the exact FlowActivation whose owner authority a later draft-write EffectAttempt must record, especially if the same version is activated more than once?
options: The Run pins the exact FlowActivation position when it starts
Each EffectAttempt reconstructs the activation from store order and the run start time
The EffectAttempt uses whichever activation is current when the send occurs
open_points.default_guess: Pin the exact FlowActivation identity or store position on the Run at start.

open_points.subject: Accepting an already accepted binding when no instance is selected
open_points.text: The accept action says “an accepted one is returned whatever the manifest says now,” while K-16 says “no binding for it can be proposed or accepted” and M28 says “a binding for it is refused when proposed or accepted” when the service has no selected instance.
open_points.question: If an accepted binding's service later has no selected instance, does another accept request return the accepted binding or refuse?
options: Return an already accepted binding; refuse only proposals and proposed-to-accepted transitions
Refuse every accept request while no instance is selected, including for an already accepted binding
Make the accepted binding lose its accepted status
open_points.default_guess: Return an already accepted binding unchanged, while refusing proposal or first acceptance without a selected instance.

open_points.subject: MCP exposure of primary actions
open_points.text: K-11 says the fixed surface consists of “inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel,” but the primary actions separately include “capture a failed execution,” “release a failed run,” “roll a slot back,” “propose an operation binding,” and “compose and prove a flow.”
open_points.question: Which MCP operations expose each primary action omitted from K-11's stated fixed set?
options: Each omitted primary action is a separate typed MCP operation
The omitted actions are variants of the listed author, run or activate operations, with an explicit mapping
The K-11 list is non-exhaustive
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as operation families and explicitly map capture, release, rollback, proposal and composition into them; add a distinct release operation if no listed family owns it.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution identity category
open_points.text: M23 declares “Identity: value” but its evidence says “an attempt's record is issued once,” while M07 says an execution observation issued once is an entity and M26 classifies an attempt as an entity.
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution a content-derived value or an occurrence entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number?
options: An entity with the composite attempt coordinates as its identity
An entity with a separately minted identifier
A value whose identity is a digest of all meaning facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by its composite attempt coordinates.
